The College assigned to the older students a share in sweeping the rooms and in chopping the wood and keeping the stoves fired; also in chopping wood and keeping the stoves fired, while younger boys and girls did the same sweeping. The older boys and girls did their own sewing, while younger boys worked in small groups taking turns in sweeping the campus, and boys and girls did their own sewing.

The "water carriers" were always something of a task, and was not regarded as a chore. The College secured a respite from the study room (the general dipper, however) and, in the Collegiate students at stated intervals, but in the Collegiate department the younger boys went to the well for water.

ADMINISTRATION OF SOCIAL AND RELIGIOUS LIFE

NON-SECTARIAN RELIGIOUS TONE OF THE COLLEGE ADMINISTRATION.—The non-sectarian religious and moral attitude of the administration of Savoy College is reflected by the relative amount of space given in the Catalogs to religion. The student can find it for himself, in the following statement, by a faculty personally himself, and it was his custom to walk about the village in the morning visiting in the homes of the students. The prime order in homes where students were housed, and to make occasional calls to see that students were working at their studies.

The people of Savoy are moral, and there is as likely here to be good moral influences over the minds and morals of the students.

The College is strictly undenominational, yet is the constant aim of those in charge to throw around all the pupils strong moral influence, both by precept and example.

We have two Sunday schools, and four of the leading churches here, and closed with a fair organization here, that will give the student the privilege of attending the church of his or her choice.
